findings.claim: The marker's start_ticks (wave 28e) is parsed from the same Get-ProcessStartIso 'o' string that start_time carries, so it adds no resolution over the start_time comparison; the flush-lock record still stores only pid+start_time. A pid reused by a process with an identical creation timestamp (coarse creation clock) is judged as the dead owner: the marker refuses and producers drop counted events, the lock is never taken over and reports stuck until the impostor exits or the operator deletes the lock.
findings.trigger: A -Forget marker or .flush.lock of a dead owner whose pid has been reused by a new process whose creation time equals the recorded one.

evidence.observation: Get-ProcessStartTicks parses ticks out of Get-ProcessStartIso's ISO string; Get-PidIdentityTicks compares them for exact equality on Windows - the same information Test-SameStartTime compares as strings (150-159).
The flush-lock record is {pid, start_time, token, since} - no start_ticks - and is judged by Test-PidAlive on the start_time string.
Two process creation FILETIMEs can collide on a coarse clock; not reproduced here.

findings.verification: RC2 (spawn 500 short-lived processes and look for equal start-time ticks on distinct pids); plus a harness case that writes a lock whose pid is live with another start time vs the same start time and observes 'gone' vs 'alive'.
findings.remedy: Record and compare 100-ns ticks read independently of the ISO string, give the flush-lock record the same start_ticks field as the marker, and surface an unconfirmable identity in -Status instead of silently counting it alive forever.

findings.claim: Remove-TelemetrySpoolLines' Windows PowerShell 5.1 fallback ([IO.File]::Replace) is not one atomic step and, unlike Write-TextAtomic, has no branch for a missing destination - a destination that vanished would make the replace fail after 8 retries and leave delivered lines to be resent.
findings.trigger: PS 5.1 where Add-Type/MoveFileEx is unavailable and the spool destination is missing at replace time.

evidence.observation: The rewrite falls straight through to File.Replace; Write-TextAtomic has an extra File.Move branch when the destination does not exist and documents Replace as not one atomic step.
The destination was just read under the telemetry lock, so it vanishing mid-rewrite is only reachable via operator interference; not run.

findings.verification: RC3: call Remove-TelemetrySpoolLines with the native move stubbed off against a path deleted after read; observe File.Replace erroring instead of recreating the file.
findings.remedy: Port Write-TextAtomic's missing-destination branch into the rewrite (and note the fallback's non-atomicity in its own comment), or fail fast when the native move cannot be prepared.

findings.claim: Exit-TelemetryFlushLock deletes the lock after its read handle is disposed, so a manual lock deletion between the token read and the delete can make a sender remove a successor's lock; the takeover path avoids this by deleting while the handle is held.
findings.trigger: The operator deletes .flush.lock in the exact window between one sender's token read and its delete, with another sender creating its lock in between.

evidence.observation: The stream is disposed in the inner finally; [IO.File]::Delete($Path) runs afterwards, outside any handle.
The takeover deletes under the still-open FileShare.Delete handle ('nobody writes it meanwhile').

findings.verification: A two-process test racing Exit-TelemetryFlushLock against a manual lock-file replacement; observe the successor's lock disappearing.
findings.remedy: Delete the lock while its handle is still open (FileShare.Delete), as the takeover does.

findings.claim: The repeated inline ask for a multi-line -Prompt keeps only the first non-blank line (whitespace folded, cut at 300 chars with a pointer to the top of the prompt) plus a line count; after a compaction that dropped the prompt top, the repeated line neither carries the rest of the ask nor a useful pointer. A documented limitation (comment 4131-35), not a regression of D7.
findings.trigger: A context_tokens member running without a brief file, a multi-line -Prompt whose first line exceeds 300 characters, and a mid-review compaction.

evidence.observation: $askLines[0] only, cut at 300 with '(cut here: the whole ask is at the top of this prompt)' and '(+N more lines)'.
REREAD covers the one-line and the cut-at-300 cases, not the post-compaction usefulness of the repeated line.

findings.verification: Run the REREAD case with a multi-line prompt whose first line is >300 chars and assert on the exact repeated tail line.
findings.remedy: Repeat the full ask (bounded), or write the ask to a small file and point the tail line at that file.
